chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
My father said to me one day during his illness: “My son, bring in some men from Quraysh from the people of al-Madīnah so that I may make them witnesses.”
He said: “So I brought some of them in to him, and he said: O Jaʿfar, when I die, then wash me, shroud me, raise my grave by four fingers, and sprinkle it with water.”

When they left, I said: “My father, if you had ordered me with this, I would have done it. Why did you want me to bring people in to you as witnesses?” He said: “My son, I wanted that you should not be disputed with.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعَ أَصَابِعَ: the measure of four fingers for raising the grave
key_terms.أُشْهِدَهُمْ: to make them witnesses over the instruction
key_terms.فَغَسِّلْنِي: wash me after death with ghusl
key_terms.كَفِّنِّي: shroud me in the burial cloth
key_terms.لَا تُنَازَعَ: so that no one would contest or dispute with you

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam gather witnesses for his funeral instructions before his death?
ai.summary: This hadith relates the final instructions of the father of Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام concerning his funeral rites and grave. It highlights practical rulings regarding washing, shrouding, grave elevation, and sprinkling water, while also showing the importance of public witness to prevent later dispute.
